t: The richest city of archaic Ionia, at the mouth of the Maeander, with its own oracle of Apollo at Didyma.
Milesian colonists founded dozens of settlements around the Black Sea, and Thales and his successors began Greek philosophy there.
Miletus led the Ionian Revolt against Persia and was sacked in 494 BCE, a disaster that led to the Persian Wars.
dyk: The Athenian playwright Phrynichus was fined for staging The Capture of Miletus, because the play reminded Athenians of the disaster to their Ionian kin.
ev: Ionian Greeks settle Miletus, traditionally under Neleus, son of Codrus
Thrasybulus makes peace with Alyattes of Lydia after eleven years of war
Miletus alone among Ionian cities gains a treaty with Cyrus the Great
Aristagoras launches the Ionian Revolt against the Achaemenid Empire
Persia defeats the Ionians at the Battle of Lade and sacks Miletus
Miletus is freed after the Battle of Mycale and rebuilt on a grid plan
Alexander the Great takes Miletus after a siege
Bequest of Attalus III brings Miletus under Roman supremacy in Asia

f.founder: Ionian settlers (traditional founder Neleus, son of Codrus)
